identity.name: Sodium sorbate
identity.chemical_class: Sorbic acid sodium salt (unsaturated aliphatic carboxylate preservative)

function.mechanism: Sorbate preservatives inhibit growth of spoilage microorganisms (especially yeasts/moulds) in acidic food systems; efficacy depends on matrix and concentration.

adi.basis: No EFSA ADI specifically identified for sodium sorbate (E201); EFSA ADIs in 2015 and 2019 were set for sorbic acid (E200) and potassium sorbate (E202).

efsa.key_finding: EFSA re-evaluation context reported possible genotoxicity concern for sodium sorbate in 2015 and did not include it in the group ADI; 2019 follow-up established 11 mg/kg bw/day group ADI for E200/E202.

adi.basis: Group ADI 0-25 mg/kg bw (expressed as sorbic acid) for sorbic acid and calcium, potassium, and sodium salts.

concerns.summary: Mixed genotoxicity literature: several older studies were negative for sorbic acid/potassium sorbate, while weak clastogenic effects were reported for stored sodium sorbate and one in-vitro human lymphocyte study reported genotoxic effects at higher concentrations.
Observational epidemiology found an association between potassium sorbate exposure and higher type 2 diabetes incidence in a large French cohort; causality is not established.
No direct IARC carcinogenic classification for sodium sorbate was identified in the current IARC classifications dataset.

no_concern_confirmed: FDA lists sodium sorbate as GRAS under 21 CFR 182.3795 when used per GMP.
JECFA maintains a group ADI (0-25 mg/kg bw as sorbic acid) including sodium sorbate.

populations: toddlers and children in earlier EFSA temporary ADI scenarios for sorbates
high consumers of preservative-rich processed foods
adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA 2019 indicates non-brand-loyal high estimates (children 95th percentile 3.7 mg/kg bw/day) did not exceed the updated 11 mg/kg bw/day ADI for E200/E202; E201-specific EFSA ADI was not identified.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory acceptance persists (FDA GRAS, JECFA group ADI), but EFSA re-evaluation context flagged sodium sorbate genotoxicity concern and excluded it from group ADI framing; combined with mixed genotoxic data and emerging observational signals, this supports a cautious moderate tier rather than limited or high.
key_factors: FDA GRAS status under GMP with specific CFR citation
JECFA group ADI includes sodium sorbate
EFSA 2015 concern on sodium sorbate genotoxicity and no clear E201-specific ADI
